_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::structural_mechanics#2 — the isogeometric 2D cell type is WALLNURBS, not WALL, and the diagnostic for the wrong spelling blames the wrong thing. Three arms on the upstream deck tests/input_files/w1_w1nurbs.4C.yaml, which is the ideal witness because one mesh carries BOTH families: four 'WALLNURBS NURBS9' cells on CP control points and four 'WALL QUAD4' cells on plain NODE lines. Run 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev (git 89519cf) at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C. Observed: the untouched deck exits 0 with 'processor 0 finished normally' and BASE_HAS_PLAIN_WALL_ELEMENTS=4, so WALL is a registered element type in the very same run in which rewriting 'WALLNURBS NURBS9' as 'WALL NURBS9' aborts with "Unknown type 'WALL' of finite element" from core/comm/4C_comm_parobjectfactory.cpp line 153 — what is unregistered is the WALL-plus-NURBS pairing, not WALL. The third arm is the silent one: rewriting exactly the 16 'CP <id> COORD x y z <weight>' lines as ordinary 'NODE <id> COORD x y z', deck otherwise untouched with SHAPEFCT: "Nurbs" and STRUCTURE KNOTVECTORS still in place, SEGFAULTS inside Wall1::w1_nlnstiffmass — shell status 139, NODELINES_FOURC_ERROR_BLOCKS=0, no error block, only the MPI signal line. The presence of every string this fixture edits is asserted first, so an upstream rename breaks it loudly instead of voiding it.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology from the second arm: leave WALLNURBS alone. The parobjectfactory abort disappears and EXIT_WALLNURBS becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the pathology from the third arm: hand it the pristine deck, CP control-point lines intact. The segfault disappears and EXIT_NODELINES becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
